messages:
Leah (AE): Heads-up team — CometFin (large payments platform) emailed a 108-question RFI + capability/compliance matrix. Deadline next Wed COB. They want: technical answers, security questionnaire, POC SOW (3-week) and a pricing band for Dedicated vs Private + sample SLA and escrow wording. I dropped the spreadsheet: /shared/cometfin/rfi/cometfin_rfi_108.xlsx. Can we divvy?

Dev (SE): I can own the capability matrix and perf numbers. Quick clarifier: they ask about "edge inference" and deploying model shards into customer datacenters. We support Private + local inference nodes — should we note constraints?

Leah (AE): Yes, they specifically asked about hybrid edge for low-latency ATM verification. Say Private supports on-prem nodes with local KV cache and model shards; requires a Private license and an ops integration piece.

Rita (Security): I'll take the security questionnaire and compliance matrix. There are PCI, SOC2, FedRAMP-lite questions and a custom data-provenance row. I'll draft standard answers and flag legal items (export controls, escrow language).

Jon (Solutions): I'll own the POC SOW and the demo checklist — they want an instrumentation runbook and a sample telemetry dashboard screenshot for Console. I can create a sanitized dashboard image and a metrics checklist (latency percentiles, token-cost, error-rate).

Dev (SE): Technical draft snippets: "Function calling & structured outputs: Supported on Hosted and Dedicated; Private supports it with runtime >=2.1 and control-plane allowlist. Quantization (int8/int4): Supported on Dedicated and Private with validated profiles; Hosted availability per model in catalog. Edge shards: Supported for Private with an ops integration; model shard residency requires customer-provided storage and network ACLs."

Rita (Security): Security draft snippets: "Transport TLS1.2+ (TLS1.3 preferred), AES-256 at rest, per-tenant encryption keys, optional BYOK via AWS KMS/Azure Key Vault, HSM appliances supported in Private. Logs: For Private, logs stay customer-controlled; for Hosted/Dedicated we provide tenant-scoped logs with RBAC and optional export to customer S3/GCS. Access to logs is limited to authorized ops with audited access approvals."

Rita (Security): Flagging these rows for Legal: 1) escrow of model weights and code, 2) export control / dual-use question, 3) vendor indemnity for open-source model licenses. Hal (Legal) — can you review when I tag?

Hal (Legal): On it. For escrow we usually provide a limited-source snapshot subject to NDA and escrow fees; will draft a short escalation note. For model license indemnity we should add a caveat: Redwood cannot extend vendor indemnities; we will coordinate but recommend a separate schedule if customer needs indemnity.

Jon (Solutions): POC SOW (3-week) draft: "Week 0 (provisioning): VPC peering, IAM, KMS test, edge node creds. Week 1 (baseline): ingest sample corpus, run embedding and gen baselines, collect perf/latency at 100/500/1000 QPS. Week 2 (validation): security verifications, provenance & redaction tests, optional Private edge shard smoke. Deliverables: perf report, telemetry dashboard, runbook, model/quantization recommendation."

Dev (SE): Throughput quick estimates for their sample traffic (70% embeds @ 300 tokens, 30% gen @ 1k tokens): 100 QPS -> ~40k tks/s; 500 QPS -> ~200k tks/s; 1000 QPS -> ~400k tks/s. I'll attach a tiny table in the matrix.

Leah (AE): Pricing ask: Jon/Jon— include pricing ranges for 3-week POC Dedicated baseline, optional Private week, edge node installation fee, and on-site audit. Also add a line for escrow + legal review fees.

Jon (Solutions): I'll sketch pricing bands: baseline POC (Dedicated) estimated $xxk-yyk for 3 weeks, Private evaluation week add-on $zzk, edge node installation one-time fee $ak, on-site audit/day rate $bk. Exact numbers after Dev confirms perf sizing.

Rita (Security): PCI note: We do not provide Hosted PCI attestation out-of-the-box. Proposed answer: "We support PCI-compliant architectures (Private or Dedicated with hardened controls); formal PCI attestation requires a scoped engagement and may require network segmentation and a third-party assessor." Tagging Hal for legal escalation text.

Hal (Legal): I'll draft the escrow + PCI escalation language and a short paragraph on indemnity and export control assumptions. Expect a draft by Tue EOD.

Leah (AE): Upload plan: capability_matrix_filled.xlsx (Dev), security_answers_cometfin.docx (Rita), poc_sow_cometfin.pdf (Jon), pricing_band_cometfin.csv (Jon), telemetry_dashboard.png (Jon). Place into /shared/cometfin/rfi/submission_bundle/. I'll zip after sign-offs.

uploader-bot: Snapshot created: https://drive.internal/s/cometfin/rfi/submission_bundle/ — will update when files are uploaded :white_check_mark:

Dev (SE): A couple internal notes for the matrix: 1) failover behavior: "Smart routing to alternates or lower-cost compatible models; customers may pin models to avoid fallback." 2) SLA blurb: "Dedicated reserved pools: 99.95% availability for committed capacity; burst best-effort subject to region capacity with automatic graceful fallback. SLA credits defined in contract."

Jon (Solutions): Demo checklist I'll include: latency p50/p95/p99, token cost per route, embedding recall sample, provenance header in responses, function-call success rate, and a small regression test set.

Rita (Security): Timeline: I'll have security draft by Tue 11am PT with inline legal flags; Dev — matrix by Tue 2pm PT; Jon — POC & pricing by Tue 4pm PT; Hal — legal escalation draft Tue EOD. Leah will consolidate Wed morning for final review.

Leah (AE): Thanks team. If anything high-risk comes up, tag @Hal immediately. I'll own the final submission and the cover email.
